title: Lost Mexico City job; Howard Walker's bus band leaves for Minnesota
summary: A $20-a-night Mexico City job collapses when the track is blown up; back home, Howard Walker rehearses a band two weeks and heads north, playing dances along the way.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: They're good musicians and they got the music ranged up. Were you ready? Towards last, yeah. Towards last they had got a good job before they blew up that track there. We were going to Mexico City. I had done practiced up with the band. They had a good job there. Twenty dollars a night, all expense paid. Just stay right in the hotel. And tips. Oh, I'd have had some do when I come back there. So the fella had done, made the contract some kind of way. And shortly after that, that's why they blew up the track at Victoria. And then that bust up the trip. And I didn't get a chance to go. That's why I wanted to come home. I just gusted them, you know, that big job there. Twenty dollars a night. No expense. That money's safe. And then tips are so good over there. You make over fifteen or twenty dollars a night tips. That's why I come out of there and come back here. And the time I got back here, Howard Walker come down there with his big old bus. He was getting the band to go to Minnesota. St. Paul, Minnesota. And we picked up some musicians in Jackson, Mississippi. And Memphis. And the entertainer went back to Elligrano for two weeks rehearsing. We rehearsed for two weeks, got the band in shape and left. By the way, St. Louis, we give a dance in Bligh, Arkansas. You know, we'd wake all the way going up. Bligh, Arkansas, and then we went to St. Louis. We'd give a dance in St. Louis. Imperial, Illinois. We'd give a dance there.
